title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **A\*** | A path search that expands the most promising cell first, using the cost so far plus an estimate of the cost remaining. (4.05) |
| **AABB** | Axis-aligned bounding box: a rectangle (or box in 3D) whose sides are parallel to the axes. (3.01) |
| **Accumulator** | In a fixed-step loop, the real time that has passed but has not been simulated yet. (3.04) |
| **Additive blending** | Drawing where colours add up, so overlaps glow brighter; used for fire, sparks and light. (4.03) |
| **Alpha** | A colour's opacity, 0 (invisible) to 255 (solid). In interpolation, how far between two steps the current time is. (1.03, 3.04) |
| **Atlas** | One texture holding many smaller pictures, such as the glyphs of a font or the tiles of a level. (2.03) |
| **Auto-tiling** | Choosing a wall's picture automatically from which of its neighbours are walls. (4.02) |
| **BFS** | Breadth-first search: explores cells in order of distance, finding shortest paths when every step costs the same. (4.05) |
| **Broad phase** | The cheap first step of collision detection that finds which pairs might touch. (3.05) |
| **Camera2D / Camera3D** | raylib's descriptions of which part of the world is shown and how. (4.01, 5.01) |
| **Checksum** | A number computed from a file's contents and stored with it, to detect damage. (6.01) |
| **Coyote time** | A short time after leaving a ledge during which a jump is still allowed. (3.03) |
| **Dead zone** | A range of input treated as zero (stick drift), or a box the player can move in without the camera following. (1.05, 4.01) |
| **Delta time (dt)** | The time the last frame took, used to make movement per second instead of per frame. (1.04) |
| **Dot product** | `a · b`: how much two directions agree; for normalised vectors, the cosine of the angle between them. (5.01) |
| **Emitter** | Something that creates particles, in bursts or at a steady rate. (4.03) |
| **Emscripten** | The compiler that turns C and C++ into WebAssembly so a game runs in a browser. (6.02) |
| **Fixed time step** | Simulating in equal steps regardless of the frame rate. (3.04) |
| **Flow field** | A grid of distances to one target, which any number of units can follow downhill. (4.05) |
| **Fragment shader** | A GPU program that runs once per pixel and chooses its colour. (5.04) |
| **Frame** | One pass of input, update and draw. (1.02) |
| **Game loop** | The loop every game runs: read input, update the world, draw it. (1.02) |
| **Jump buffering** | Remembering a jump press for a short time so it happens as soon as the player lands. (3.03) |
| **Juice** | Small effects that change how a game feels but not its rules: shake, flashes, particles, sounds. (4.03) |
| **Letterbox** | Scaling a picture to fit the screen and filling the rest with bars. (2.01, 5.05) |
| **Migration** | Converting data saved by an older version of the game into the current format. (6.01) |
| **Minimum translation vector** | The shortest move that separates two overlapping shapes. (3.02) |
| **Narrow phase** | The exact collision test, run only on the pairs the broad phase found. (3.05) |
| **Normal** | A direction perpendicular to a surface, pointing out of it. (3.02, 5.03) |
| **Parallax** | Background layers moving slower than the world to suggest depth. (4.01) |
| **Particle** | A small, short-lived object with a position, velocity and lifetime. (4.03) |
| **Pitch / yaw** | Looking up and down / turning left and right. (5.02) |
| **Pool** | A fixed block of pre-allocated objects reused instead of creating and destroying them. (4.03) |
| **Post-processing** | A shader applied to the whole finished frame. (5.05) |
| **Ray** | A start point and a direction; ray tests answer "what is in this direction?". (5.03) |
| **Render texture** | A texture you can draw into instead of the screen. (5.05) |
| **Semi-implicit Euler** | Updating velocity from acceleration first, then position from the new velocity. (1.04) |
| **Shader** | A small program that runs on the GPU for every vertex or pixel. (5.04) |
| **Slab method** | Testing a ray against a box as the overlap of three pairs of parallel planes. (5.03) |
| **Sound alias** | A second Sound that shares another's sample data, so both can play at once. (2.04) |
| **Spatial grid** | Cells that list the objects inside them, so only nearby objects are tested against each other. (3.05) |
| **Spiral of death** | Simulation steps taking longer than real time, making each frame slower than the last. (3.04) |
| **Sprite sheet** | One texture holding the frames of animations in a grid. (2.02) |
| **State machine** | A set of states, exactly one of them current, and the events that move between them. (2.05, 4.04) |
| **Swap and pop** | Removing an element by moving the last one into its place, when order does not matter. (4.03) |
| **Telegraphing** | Showing that an attack is coming so the player can react. (4.04) |
| **Texture2D** | A picture in video memory, ready to draw. (2.01) |
| **Tile map** | A grid of tile numbers describing a level. (4.02) |
| **Tint** | A colour multiplied into every pixel of a drawn texture. (2.01) |
| **Trauma** | A 0 to 1 value that events add to, driving screen shake. (4.01) |
| **Tunnelling** | A fast object passing completely through a thin one between two frames. (3.02) |
| **Uniform** | A value passed to a shader that is the same for every pixel of a draw call. (5.04) |
| **Working directory** | The folder relative paths start from; often not the folder of the .exe. (2.01, 6.02) |
